title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on "Five Prohibitions" and the Measures for Handling Violations of the Provisions on "Five Prohibitions"
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the "Five Prohibitions" and

the Measures for Handling Violations of the "Five Prohibitions"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 2

All local people's courts at various levels, military courts at all levels, railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, maritime courts, and courts at all levels in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on the 'Five Prohibitions'" and the "Measures for Handling Violations of the 'Five Prohibitions'" have been discussed and adopted by the Leading Party Members Group of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

January 8, 2009

Supreme People's Court

Provisions on the "Five Prohibitions"

(Effective as of January 8, 2009)

1. It is strictly prohibited to accept invitations to meals, gifts, or other benefits from parties to a case or relevant persons.

2. It is strictly prohibited to engage in improper dealings with lawyers in violation of regulations.

3. It is strictly prohibited to interfere in or inquire about cases being handled by others.

4. It is strictly prohibited to engage in malpractice for personal gain in activities such as entrusting evaluations, auctions, etc.

5. It is strictly prohibited to divulge trial work secrets.

Any personnel of a people's court who violates the above provisions shall be investigated for disciplinary responsibility or even criminal liability in accordance with discipline and law. Those engaged in adjudication or enforcement work shall be transferred away from adjudication or enforcement posts.

Supreme People's Court

Measures for Handling Violations of the "Five Prohibitions"

Article 1 These Measures are formulated to strictly enforce the work discipline of the people's courts and ensure the implementation of the "Five Prohibitions."

Article 2 The term "accepting invitations to meals, gifts, or other benefits from parties to a case or relevant persons" as used in the "Five Prohibitions" refers to accepting money, goods, invitations to meals, entertainment, travel, or other benefits from parties to a case, defenders, agents, or personnel of entities entrusted to conduct audits, evaluations, auctions, sales, appraisals, or bankruptcy administration.

Article 3 The term "engaging in improper dealings with lawyers in violation of regulations" as used in the "Five Prohibitions" refers to engaging in improper dealings with lawyers in violation of the "Several Provisions on Regulating the Relationship Between Judges and Lawyers to Safeguard Judicial Fairness" jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice, as well as the relevant institutional provisions of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4 The term "interfering in or inquiring about cases being handled by others" as used in the "Five Prohibitions" refers to interfering, intervening, inquiring about, or soliciting information on cases handled by others in violation of regulations, or making requests or interceding with the leaders of the case-handling unit (department), members of the collegial panel, sole adjudicators, or other auxiliary case-handling personnel.

Article 5 The term "engaging in malpractice for personal gain in activities such as entrusting evaluations, auctions, etc." as used in the "Five Prohibitions" refers to engaging in favoritism or seeking personal gain in activities such as entrusting audits, evaluations, auctions, sales, appraisals, or designating bankruptcy administrators; maliciously colluding with relevant institutions and personnel; engaging in fraud; or conducting operations in violation of regulations.

Article 6 The term "divulging trial work secrets" as used in the "Five Prohibitions" refers to divulging the specific circumstances of discussions by the collegial panel or the adjudication committee on cases, or other secrets of adjudication or enforcement work, in violation of regulations.

Article 7 Personnel of a people's court under administrative staffing or institutional staffing who violate any of the "Five Prohibitions" shall be investigated for disciplinary responsibility or even criminal liability in accordance with discipline and law. Those engaged in adjudication or enforcement work shall be transferred away from adjudication or enforcement posts.

Personnel employed on a contractual basis by the people's court who violate any of the "Five Prohibitions" shall have their employment contracts terminated.

Article 8 Clues regarding violations of the "Five Prohibitions" by personnel of the people's court shall be managed uniformly by the disciplinary inspection and supervision department of the people's court. If other departments of the people's court receive reports from the public or discover clues on their own, they shall promptly transfer them to the disciplinary inspection and supervision department.

Article 9 The disciplinary inspection and supervision department of a people's court shall promptly verify clues regarding violations of the "Five Prohibitions" within its jurisdiction. Once verified, if it is necessary to transfer the person from the adjudication or enforcement post, it shall promptly submit a handling proposal to the Leading Party Members Group of the court for decision.

Article 10 The personnel department of the people's court shall, based on the decision of the Leading Party Members Group, carry out organizational processing procedures for persons who violate the "Five Prohibitions."

Article 11 If a person who violates the "Five Prohibitions" needs to be investigated for disciplinary responsibility, the disciplinary inspection and supervision department and the party organization of the court shall handle it separately in accordance with procedures; if criminal liability needs to be pursued, the disciplinary inspection and supervision department shall be responsible for transferring the case to the relevant judicial department.

Article 12 Persons who have been sanctioned for violating the "Five Prohibitions" shall have their annual assessment grade determined as "unqualified."

Article 13 These Measures shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 14 These Measures shall take effect from the date of promulgation.
